units.la: XI. Non sunt Signa nuda, sed Communio corporis & sanguinis Christi: hujus inquam Communionis non saltem signa significantia & adumbrantia, sed & sigilla, &c, si velis, etiam Instrumenta sano sensu, scil. Moralia non Physica: & multò minùs corporis & sanguinis Christi ὀχήματα.
units.tr: XI. They are not bare signs, but the communion of the body and blood of Christ. Of this communion they are not only signs signifying and foreshadowing it, but also seals, etc., and, if you wish, even instruments in a sound sense, namely moral and not physical; and by much less are they vehicles [ὀχήματα] of the body and blood of Christ.

units.la: XXXV.
units.tr: XXXV.

units.la: XII. Corpus & sanguis Christi in Coena non sunt signum, sed Res signata: de his enim Apostolus contradistinctè loquitur ad signa, quae sunt Calix & Panis.
units.tr: XII. The body and blood of Christ in the Supper are not the sign but the thing signified. For the Apostle speaks of these in contrast with the signs, which are the cup and the bread.

units.la: XXXVI.
units.tr: XXXVI.

units.la: XIII. In Coena duplex est communio: Fidelium videlicet cum Christo, cujus corpus & sanguinem participantes, cum ipso uniuntur: & Fidelium inter se, idem pabulum participantium.
units.tr: XIII. In the Supper there is a twofold communion: that of the faithful with Christ, in that by partaking of his body and blood they are united with him; and that of the faithful among themselves, as they partake of the same food.

units.la: XXXVII.
units.tr: XXXVII.

units.la: XIV. In communione cum Christo non saltem vim meriti & beneficia, sed & Corpus ipsum participamus.
units.tr: XIV. In communion with Christ we partake not only of the power of his merit and his benefits, but also of the body itself.

units.la: XXXVIII.
units.tr: XXXVIII.

units.la: XV. Communio haec nonnisi spiritualis est, hincque nomen alia datur corporis Christi manducatio. vid. Quaest. 14, 15.
units.tr: XV. This communion is only spiritual, and for this reason the eating of the body of Christ is also called by another name. See Questions 14 and 15.

units.la: XXXIX.
units.tr: XXXIX.

units.la: XVI. Communionis, quam habemus invicem, fundamentum est comunio cum Christo: ex nexu v. 16. & 17. XL. XVII. Communio fidelium inter se, & quæ inde proficiscitur, charitas & Pax mutua, usu Cœnæ significatur & fovetur. v. 17. Ad præstantissimum atq; amicissimum Dominum DEFENDENTEM.
units.tr: XVI. The fellowship which we have with one another is grounded in communion with Christ, from the connection of verses 16 and 17. XL. XVII. The communion of the faithful among themselves, and the love and mutual peace that proceed from it, are signified and nourished by the use of the Supper (v. 17). To the most excellent and most friendly Lord, the DEFENDER.

units.la: Ὡς δείπνυ Χριστὸ μυστήρια ἡμῖν ἀποφαίνεις, Παύλου ἐξευνίζας, τῷ μάλα Χριστὸς ἐπὶ Χριστὸς ἐπὶ ψυχῇ, πίστῳ σοι εὔχομαι ἐπεῖναι, Ὡς εἰκὼν μεγάλυσεῦ πατρὸς ἡς αἰ ἐν.
units.tr: As you unfold to us the mysteries of Christ's Supper, explaining the teaching of Paul, Christ is present. May Christ, I pray, be present to your faithful soul, so that you may always be the image of the great Father. [Ὡς δείπνυ Χριστὸ μυστήρια ἡμῖν ἀποφαίνεις, Παύλου ἐξευνίζας, τῷ μάλα Χριστὸς ἐπὶ Χριστὸς ἐπὶ ψυχῇ, πίστῳ σοι εὔχομαι ἐπεῖναι, Ὡς εἰκὼν μεγάλυσεῦ πατρὸς ἡς αἰ ἐν.]

units.la: Versio.
units.tr: Translation.

units.la: DUm Cœnæ Christi nobis mysteria pandis, Et Pauli explanas dogmata, Christus adest. Menti Christus adest, adsit precor Ipse fideli, Ut sis Magnifici semper imago Patris.
units.tr: While you set forth for us the mysteries of Christ's Supper and explain the doctrines of Paul, Christ is present. Christ is present to the mind; may he, I pray, be present to you, his faithful one, so that you may always be the image of the Magnificent Father.

units.tr: M. J. R. Wetstenius

units.la: DUm praclare tuas, CRVG I percurrere laudes, Molior, en! nimia vix traho mole pedes; Non æquare meo possum praconia versu, Per quæ sublimem te tua Fama rapit: Ardua namq; via est dignis extollere verbis Virtutem, pedibus nec satis apta meis: Ipsa sibi decus est, pulchris reverentia factis Splendet & obscurum nil sinit esse sui. Es similis Patri, sequerisq; per omnia Patrem, Ingenium Patris est, fulget ab ore Pater; Omnia sunt Patris, quid prodest dicere plura? Vita, animus, mores, & pietatis amor. Non eget exigua tam splendida gloria laudis, Plus laudasse parum, quàm tacuisse, nocet.
units.tr: While I undertake to run through your praises, O Crug, lo! I can scarcely drag my feet under their huge weight. I cannot match your renown with my verse, by which your Fame carries you aloft; for the way is steep to raise virtue with worthy words, and my feet are not nimble enough. Virtue is its own glory, and reverence for noble deeds shines forth and allows nothing of it to be obscure. You are like your Father, and follow your Father in all things; the Father's genius is yours, the Father shines from your face; all things are the Father's. Why say more? Life, spirit, character, and love of piety. So splendid a glory does not need a small measure of praise; to have praised too little does more harm than to have kept silent.
